resources.string: Connection refused: turn on wireless debugging, or run adb tcpip 5555 again from the PC.
Not authorized: accept the “Allow debugging” prompt in the headset, then try again.
Pairing required: pair the app with a code.
Code rejected or expired: request a new code and try again.
Wireless debugging not found: turn it back on in the developer options. No need to pair again.
Unexpected failure: try again. If it persists, turn wireless debugging off and on again.
Pairing code (if your headset offers it)
Open the developer options and turn on “Wireless debugging”.
Tap “Pair device with pairing code”, keep that panel next to this one, then enter the port and code below.
Couldn\'t open them automatically: go through the headset settings (Settings → System → Developer) or the Android developer options.
Leave empty to find it automatically.
Plug the headset into a computer with ADB and run:
Unplug the cable, tap “Connect (via PC)”, then accept the debugging prompt in the headset (“Always allow”).
Only once: then tap “Switch to wireless” and you won\'t need the PC anymore.
Some Horizon OS versions don\'t show this screen. In that case, do the first connection with a PC, then “Switch to wireless”.
The headset may ask you to allow wireless debugging on this network: check “Always allow”.
Waiting for the network authorization in the headset…
Network not allowed in time: try again and accept the Horizon OS window.
The wireless connection failed. Try again in a moment.
No VR game found on this headset. Install a game, then tap Refresh.
Unrecognized headset: Quest 3 values are offered and every setting is experimental.
×1.0 is the headset default: %1$d×%2$d pixels per eye.
Above level %1$d, the headset only grants this level under conditions (passthrough off, among others); otherwise it stays capped.
Heat and battery: high CPU/GPU levels or a resolution above ×1.0 make the headset warmer and shorten battery life.
Smoothness: such a high resolution can make the frame rate drop.
Applied settings stay active after the game closes, including for games launched from the Quest menu, until “Reset all” or a headset restart.
Connect the app to the headset to launch the game. You can still save the profile.
The profile could not be saved.
Game launched. Settings stay active until “Reset all” or a headset restart.
The “%1$s” setting could not be applied: the game was not launched.
The game could not be stopped: it was not launched.
Settings applied, but the game could not be launched.
Game not found: it may have been uninstalled. The list has been refreshed.
Values not supported by this headset: %1$s. Edit the profile.
Connection lost: reconnect the app and try again.
Sets the 7 settings active on the headset back to their defaults, for every game. Your saved profiles are kept and applied again at the next launch from the app.
Connect the app to reset. A headset restart also clears every setting.
Headset settings are back to their defaults. Your profiles are kept.
Reset incomplete for: %1$s. Try again, or restart the headset.
Launching is disabled: the app is not connected to the headset.
Every setting of “%1$s” will go back to “Game default”. Settings already applied to the headset stay active until “Reset all” or a restart.
The profile could not be deleted.
Saved profile for this game: it is applied to the headset at each launch from OpenQuestTuner.
The headset is hot (state: %1$s). The system may lower performance: lower the CPU/GPU levels or the resolution, or take a break.
Connect the app to read the settings active on the headset.
Active settings cannot be read right now.
